verdict.rationale: Discord documents headless, programmatic use: a REST API, bot-token authentication, a Gateway WebSocket for events, and incoming webhooks that need no bot user or auth. Its webhook docs explicitly name CI/CD pipelines posting build results as a use case. Headless use is limited to API-driven integrations rather than running the product itself without a UI; there is no official CLI or headless client mode, and the OpenAPI spec is only a preview. Missing for 10: an official CLI or headless runner, documented CI-specific guidance beyond posting notifications, a stable machine-readable spec, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: CI/CD pipelines posting build results or deployment notifications
The Discord API is a REST API that allows you to interact with Discord data from your own applications.
Authenticating with the Discord API can be done in one of two ways: 1. Using a bot token... 2. Using an OAuth2 bearer token
They do not require a bot user or authentication to use.
The Gateway API lets apps open secure WebSocket connections with Discord to receive events about actions that take place in a server/guild
